records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
records.flowers: Terminal head-like cluster; calyx teeth acuminate 1–2 mm; lavender, rarely white corolla with tube 15–24 mm; genus: 2 stamens
records.habitat: Stream banks, hillsides, prairies, open woods or open ground
records.taxon_caveat: Flora treatment explicitly applies to var. mollis; not necessarily all M. fistulosa. Kew recognizes var. mollis within species.

records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
records.habit: Annual or short-lived perennial, branched, to 100 cm
records.flowers: Yellow to cream, white or rarely pink corollas usually with reddish-brown dots; flower heads in interrupted spikes; calyx teeth short triangular not bristle-tipped (genus key)
records.leaves: Aromatic gland-dotted and usually toothed (genus); varieties distinguished by pubescence, leaf widths and calyx-tooth shapes
records.habitat: Sandy open woods and open ground
records.taxon_caveat: 1999 flora describes vars. intermedia, lasiodonta, occidentalis with differing morphology. Record broad species treatment only pending varietal reconciliation.

records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
records.habit: Perennial with short vertical rhizomes; stems to 2 m, usually shorter
records.leaves: Lower 1–4 nodes' petiolate leaves lost by anthesis; remaining narrowly linear to lanceolate/oblanceolate leaves usually <12 mm wide, sharply serrate, usually stem-clasping
records.flowers: Usually pale lavender/whitish corollas 22–33 mm, purple streaks/spots internally; no sterile bracts below lowest flower (key)
records.habitat: Low moist sites and roadside ditches

records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
records.habit: Perennial with short unbranched vertical rhizomes; stems to ca. 1.3 m
records.leaves: Lower petiolate leaves to 13 mm wide shed early; upper stem leaves to 6 mm wide, sharply serrate
records.flowers: Up to 40 pairs of sterile floral bracts often below lowest flower; reddish-violet, lavender or white corolla usually purple-marked inside
records.taxon_caveat: 1999 description is subsp. praemorsa ONLY, not species-wide; the flora contrasts subsp. virginiana, with much wider stem leaves (3–55 mm)

records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
records.habit: Perennial herb, stems to 1.5 m; sometimes flowers at 15 cm; retrorsely pubescent
records.flowers: Calyx 4.5–10 mm; blue corolla 15–25 mm, usually whitish center; genus key shows whorled flowers and discernible calyx teeth; 2 stamens
records.taxon_caveat: Kew synonymizes var. grandiflora under Salvia azurea; flora regional measurements may not apply throughout broad species

records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
records.leaves: Blades to 7 × 5 cm; genus key: deltoid-ovate and truncate/cordate base, petioles 10–35 mm
records.flowers: Calyx 6–9 mm, commonly reddish; lobes nearly half tube length; bright to deep red corolla 16.5–22 mm; genus: 2 stamens

records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
records.habit: Perennial herb from woody root, stems to ca. 0.4 m
records.flowers: Gaping pale lavender-blue corolla to ca. 22 mm, darker throat veins and two basal white regions on lower lip; genus key: bracts exceeding calyx, dense white bristly throat ring, corolla upper lip 10–12 mm
records.flora_distribution_note: Texas endemic according to flora; separate BONAP county proof pending

records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
records.habit: Minutely pubescent perennial, 0.25–1 m; flowering in first year, woody root developing
records.leaves: Lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, to 10 × 3 cm, shallowly toothed or entire
records.flowers: Calyces densely matted/felty white to purple pubescence, teeth obscured; violet-blue/purple corolla to 25 mm; genus: 2 stamens

records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
records.flowers: Calyx 10–15 mm; red corolla 25–30 mm; genus: 2 stamens
records.habitat: Rocky soils in central, western and southern Texas; ornamental persisted and escaped north of natural area
records.caveat: 1999 flora distinguishes native distribution from planted persistent occurrences; no Hays County BONAP conclusion

records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
records.habit: Pilose, usually scapose perennial 0.25–0.65(–0.8) m with basal rosette
records.leaves: Prominent basal leaves, sometimes deeply divided/lyrate; flowering stems with 1–2 pairs of reduced leaves
records.flowers: Simple to few-branched inflorescence; light blue-lavender corolla 20–30 mm, darker blue markings; genus: 2 stamens
